data.description:
## Context
The accepted benchmark contract on closed ticket left-changeful-mamba deliberately requires 3,000 tickets, 6,000 events, exactly 24 batched commits, and at least a 10x commit-count reduction. The test is still the integration tier long pole: 90.18s on 2026-08-01 and 93.34-107.84s on current macOS jobs, consuming 37-45% of the entire integration tier. Reducing N would violate the accepted contract and is out of scope.

## Plan
Profile import_tickets across N values only to locate scaling costs, then optimize the importer/batch persistence path while preserving N=3000 and the commit/crash-resume contracts. Prefer fewer redundant scans/serializations/git operations, not test removal or sharding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The committed benchmark remains N=3000 with 6,000 events and exactly 24 commits.
- [ ] Created/comment counts and >=10x reduction assertions remain unchanged.
- [ ] A before/after profile identifies the dominant scaling artifact and demonstrates lower runner time on the same host.
- [ ] Crash-resume and rollback suites stay green.
- [ ] No platform or Python-matrix coverage is removed.
data.title: Optimize the N=3000 import benchmark path without shrinking its contract
